# Tidepool Landing Page: Build Plan

**Design direction:** Calm, structured, and collaborative. The Library reference uses forest green, coral, and a monospace quote, so Tidepool uses a different system: deep slate-teal with sand neutrals and one warm amber accent. Type is a geometric sans for display and a humanist sans for body. No monospace.

**1. Navigation**
Sticky, slim bar. Wordmark left, three links (Product, Teams, Pricing), a "Start a shared week" button right. Background turns solid teal after scroll.

**2. Hero**
Split layout: copy left, product frame right. Headline, 10 words max: *"Plan the week together, without the group chat."* Subhead in one sentence naming the core loop: assign, see, adjust. Primary CTA plus a secondary "Watch 60-second tour" text link. Right side shows a real UI screenshot of a shared week board with three team avatars. No stock photography.

**3. Proof strip**
Single row of small-caps text: team count, average setup time, and one customer name. Sand background, no icons.

**4. Problem**
Three columns with short, blunt statements: "Tasks live in five threads," "Nobody knows who owns Thursday," "Friday arrives with nothing finished." Plain sans, no illustrations.

**5. How it works**
Three numbered steps running horizontally: Map the week, Claim the work, Check in Friday. A thin horizontal wave line divides the steps, a subtle nod to the name. Each step gets a small UI crop.

**6. Feature spotlight**
Large screenshot with three amber callouts pointing to specific controls (drag, assign, recurring). Copy is two short paragraphs. Use a rounded callout line, not a hand-drawn arrow.

**7. Testimonial**
Full-width band, pull quote in a large serif, attributed with name, role, and team size. Not a grid of avatars.

**8. Pricing**
Two cards: Team and Organization. Price per team, not per seat, stated plainly. One line under each card about who it's for.

**9. FAQ**
Five accordion items covering setup, data export, guest access, and billing.

**10. Final CTA**
Full-bleed deep teal band. One headline, one button, no secondary links.

**11. Footer**
Four link columns, privacy and status links, small wordmark.

# Tidepool Landing Page: Revised Build Plan

**Design direction:** Calm, structured, collaborative. Deep slate-teal ground, sand neutrals, one warm amber accent used only for actions and callouts. Geometric sans for display, humanist sans for body. Every text-on-background pair must meet WCAG AA, so amber never carries body copy. Mobile stacks every section to one column, with the hero screenshot following the headline.

**1. Navigation**
Slim sticky bar. Wordmark left; Product, Teams, Pricing center; "Start a shared week" button right. Transparent over the hero, solid teal after 80px of scroll.

**2. Hero**
Split layout, copy left (55%), product frame right. Headline: *"Plan the week together, without the group chat."* Subhead: *"Assign the work, see who owns what, adjust in one place."* Primary button "Start a shared week" (amber), secondary text link "Watch the 60-second tour." Right side: a real screenshot of a shared week board with three team avatars and one visibly claimed task. No stock photography.

**3. Proof strip**
Sand band, one line of text: "[X] teams planned their week in Tidepool · Average setup: [Y] minutes · Trusted by [customer name]." Use real figures only; if none exist yet, cut the strip rather than fill it with placeholders.

**4. Problem**
Three rows, not columns, each a concrete scene: "Tasks are scattered across five threads." "Thursday has no owner." "By Friday, half the list is still open." Left-aligned sans at display size, with a thin rule between rows. Copy names the reader's pain, not the product.

**5. How it works**
Three steps across a horizontal timeline: Map the week, Claim the work, Check in Friday. Days of the week appear as small dots along the line, a visual tie to planning. Each step has a 16:9 UI crop and one sentence of copy.

**6. Feature spotlight**
Large screenshot, left. Three amber numbered markers on drag-to-reschedule, assignment, and recurring tasks, each matched to a short caption in a numbered list on the right. Two sentences of intro copy maximum.

**7. Testimonial**
Full-width band, deep teal. One pull quote, large serif, about 25 words, focused on a specific outcome. Attribution: name, role, team size. No avatar grid.

**8. Pricing**
Two cards side by side. Team: price per team per month, "For households and teams up to [N] members." Organization: "Custom pricing for multi-team rollouts, with SSO and admin controls." A "Compare plans" link sits below, not a full table.

**9. FAQ**
Five accordion items: How long does setup take? Can guests join without an account? How do I export our data? What happens to our lists if we downgrade? How does billing work for teams?

**10. Final CTA**
Full-bleed amber-accented teal band. Headline: *"Make Friday's list before Monday starts."* One button, "Start a shared week." No secondary links.

**11. Footer**
Four link columns (Product, Teams, Company, Resources), privacy and status links along the bottom edge, small wordmark at left.
